headline: Approved previous meeting minutes; the chair recommended pausing changes to the discrimination reporting form while research continues.
summary: The commission heard a presentation from Shawn Newton of Salem State University on the history of the Race Equity Task Force. The chair recommended pausing changes to the Discrimination Reporting Form until the Solicitor's office finishes its research.

MINUTES OF THE RACE EQUITY COMMISSION 
September 3, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Race Equity Commission (REC) was held on September 3, 2026, at 5:00  
pm via Zoom, an online video conference call system in accordance with Chapter 2 of the Act of 
2025. Pursuant to Section 30A of chapter 20 of the acts of 2021, as amended by 2 section 40 of 
chapter 2 of the acts of 2023, and further amended by Section 1 of Chapter 2 of the Acts of 2025, 
the City is authorized to conduct remote meetings of its public bodies through June 30, 2027. 
 
 
1. Roll Call 
 
Present on the call were: Regina Zaragoza Frey (Chair), Dr. Shelby Ortega (Vice Chair), 
Dr. Vanita Naidoo, Dr. Javier Garcia -Perez, Jennifer Winsor, Human Resources Director 
Lisa Cammarata, Chief of Police Lucas Miller, and City Council Liaison Kyle Davis 
 
Absent were: Rosa Alvarado, Alexandra Ramos, Dr. Melanie Sonsteng-Person, and Salem 
Public Schools Superintendent Tommy Welch 
 
 
2. Approve previous meeting minutes. 
 
a. July 16, 2026 
 
VOTE: Motion to approve the meeting minutes for July 16, 2026 was made by 
Lisa Cammarata, seconded by Jennifer Winsor, and the motion was carried 
unanimously. 
 
 
3. Public Comment. 
 
Chair Zaragoza made a call for public comment. There was no public comment. 
 
 
4. Announcements and Updates

The next Race Equity Commission meeting falls on October 1 which is the night of the 
Haunted Happenings Parade so this meeting was rescheduled to Wednesday, September 
30 at 5:00 pm.  
 
 
5. Presentation and discussion from Salem State University’s Senior Associate Vice 
President and Dean of Students, Shawn A. Newton. 
a. History of the creation of the Race Equity Commission, 2020-2021 Race Equity 
Task Force work, the creation of the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion role 
within the City of Salem and perspectives on where race equity work should 
go. 
 
Chair Zaragoza introduced this topic by explaining that the Race Equity Task Force 
developed the Race Equity Task Force Report  with recommendations including the 
creation of the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Director position and the Race Equity 
Commission. She reported that most of the recommendations have been implemented or 
progress has been made on them. 
 
Shawn Newton introduced himself, his background in higher education, and his prior work 
with the City of Salem including chairing the No Place for Hate Committee and the Race 
Equity Task Force.  
 
He discussed the importance of defining the word “racism” at the beginning of the work of 
the Race Equity Task Force to ensure everyone was on the same page before diving into 
the work. Next, the focus was on what the issues facing the City of Salem were a nd how 
the committee can tackle them. The Task Force split into sub -groups which ended up 
informing each of the recommendations listed within the final report. There were then 
public meetings to discuss these topics and suggested recommendations.  
 
He expressed appreciation for the progress that has been made in achieving these 
recommendations laid out in the report. The City of Salem was one of the first 
municipalities to establish a task force and publish a report like this.  
 
Chair Zaragoza asked Shawn’s thoughts on how this work related to diversity, equity, and 
inclusion has changed due to the change of the federal landscape. Shawn responded by 
emphasizing the need for people to be more strategic in how they do this work and standing 
strong in these values. This will continue to be challenging to navigate.

Jennifer Winsor and Dr. Shelby Ortega asked for Shawn’s input on where the Race Equity 
Commission should focus their energy based on the work of the Race Equity Task Force 
and the final report. Shawn explained that the committee should pick one recommendation 
and really lean into them one at a time. He thinks that everyone on a commission like REC 
should feel like they’ve made a difference by the time their term has ended. The Mayor 
and City Council are relying on recommendations from REC for actions to tak e and 
initiatives to prioritize. Nothing should be off the table and everything is possible.  
 
 
6. Discussion: City Seal - Task Force recommendation, pending Council vote, and 
citizen petition to place the question on the ballot. 
 
Chair Zaragoza summarized the history of the initiative to change the City Seal. A City 
Seal Task Force was established and voted in favor to change the City Seal. After that, a 
City Council Committee considered the topic and voted in favor to change the C ity Seal. 
Next, it will go to the full City Council to vote during their next meeting on Thursday, 
September 10. REC members appreciated the summary and did not have any additional 
questions or topics to discuss. 
 
 
7. Follow up on changes to the Discrimination Reporting Form. 
a. Update from Solicitor’s office regarding changes to the form. 
 
Chair Zaragoza shared that there are now concerns about this form posing liability concerns 
for the City of Salem and their role in responding to submissions that has not been planned 
for. She met with Assistant City Solicitor Omar Bennani and shared examp les from 
Cambridge and Arlington that have similar forms.  
 
● Cambridge File a Discrimination Complaint 
● Arlington Human Rights Commission Report an Incident 
 
Bennani is going to do some research by reaching out to these communities to see how 
they monitor and respond to the forms. Chair Zaragoza recommended REC pause working 
on changes to Salem’s form until this additional research has concluded.  
 
Dr. Shelby Ortega brought up concerns about capacity and resources for the City of Salem 
compared to Cambridge and Arlington when monitoring and responding to form 
submissions. She also brought up the potential for conducting research to pilot the form if 
the group keeps being met by red tape. The process of setting up this research would require

going through the Institutional Review Board (IRB) which could provide a thorough 
review of the concerns with the form.  
 
Lisa Cammarata suggested adding information about filing discrimination complaints with 
Massachusetts Commission Against Discrimination (MCAD) to the City of Salem website 
in lieu of the City of Salem discrimination form, at least in the meantime.  
 
Dr. Vanita Naidoo shared appreciation for all of the work on this form and agreed that it 
makes sense for the next step to be focused on information gathering. Chair Zaragoza 
closed the conversation by confirming information gathering will be taking place and she 
will bring this back up in the new year with additional guidance. 
 
8. New Business. 
a. October - Hate crime and bias incident update/report by Salem Police 
Department 
b. Invite leaders of the immigrant community to share feedback, concerns, and 
establish ongoing communication with the Race Equity Commission. 
 
During the October meeting, REC will hear from a local business owner who would like 
to discuss the development of a memorial.  
 
Jennifer Winsor requested we add discussion about revisiting the Race Equity Task Force 
Report and deciding where the REC should focus their energy. 
 
No additional new business was presented. 
 
 
9. Adjournment. 
 
VOTE: Motion to adjourn was made by Jennifer Winsor, seconded by Dr. Shelby Ortega, 
and the motion was approved unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 6:28 pm.
